# A rational counterexample to the entire fiber-centroid convex hull selector

This construction does not refute OC. It disproves the stronger assertion
that an OC point can always be selected from the convex hull of all actual
positive-volume fiber centroids, intersected with the mixed-integer lattice.
Every possible convex combination is covered, not just a finite collection
of centroids, midpoint choices, or exponential-tilt barycenters.

## 1. The three exact fibers

Use coordinates (z,x,y) in R x R^2. Define

    T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)},
    A=conv{(0,0),(4/5,0),(0,8/25)},
    eta=2^(-20), s=3/128+eta,

and put

    K_-=(2-s)A, K_0=T, K_+=sA.

Let

    C=conv( ({-1} x K_-) union ({0} x K_0) union ({1} x K_+) ).

All parameters and vertices are rational. The three triangles have
positive area, and the endpoint triangles together span a full-dimensional
body in R^3. Thus C is a convex body. Its integer projection is exactly
{-1,0,1}. The endpoint fibers are exact because their indices are extreme.
The middle fiber is exactly T: homothetic convex sets satisfy

    (K_-+K_+)/2=A subset T,

and every convex combination of the three source fibers with integer
coordinate zero is a mixture of T and that endpoint midpoint body.
Hence S=C intersect (Z x R^2) consists exactly of these three fibers,
and its intrinsic dimension is q=d=2.

Write c=area(T)=1/2, a=area(K_-), b=area(K_+), and M=a+b+c.
It is convenient to put

    e=(32/125)s^2, delta=(128/125)eta.

Since area(A)/area(T)=(4/5)(8/25)=32/125, direct calculation gives

    b/c=e,
    (a-b)/c=(32/125)((2-s)^2-s^2)=1-delta,
    a/c=1+e-delta,
    M/c=2+2e-delta.                                      (1)

In particular a<c+b because delta>0. Also b<c+a. In fact all three
fibers have area strictly below M/2: c<a+b follows from 2e>delta.
For a simple certificate of these numerical ranges,

    0<eta<1/1000000,
    3/128<s<1/40,
    9/64000<=e<1/6250,
    0<delta<2/1000000.                                  (2)

These bounds imply 2e>delta immediately.

For n=1,d=2 the OC threshold is gamma_2 M/2=(2/9)M. Dividing by c,
write that threshold as

    tau=(2/9)(M/c)
       =4/9+(4/9)e-(256/1125)eta.                       (3)

## 2. All points allowed by the proposed selector

The continuous centroids are

    g_A=(4/15,8/75), g_0=(1/3,1/3),
    g_-=(2-s)g_A, g_+=s g_A.

Let

    G=conv{(-1,g_-),(0,g_0),(1,g_+)}.

Its mixed-integer points at z=-1 and z=1 are only the two endpoint
centroids. At z=0, a convex combination has equal coefficients on
the endpoint centroids. Therefore the complete remaining candidate
set is exactly

    G_0=[g_A,g_0].                                      (4)

Every point (x,y) on this segment satisfies

    x+y=(22y+4)/17.                                    (5)

Thus (4) accounts for all arbitrary centroid mixtures with integer
first coordinate. Convexity of C puts every such candidate in S.

## 3. Two fixed bad halfspaces cover the entire middle candidate segment

Define

    h=1/3-(17/52)e,
    k=(22h+4)/17=2/3-(11/26)e,
    B=(8/25)(1-s).

The elementary bounds (2) give

    8/25<h<1/3, 0<k<2/3.

Consider the two closed ambient halfspaces

    H_A={y+Bz>=h},
    H_B={x+y-2z<=k}.                                  (6)

For H_A, the maximum of y+Bz on either endpoint fiber is exactly 8/25:

    max_(K_-) y-B=(2-s)(8/25)-(1-s)(8/25)=8/25,
    max_(K_+) y+B=s(8/25)+(1-s)(8/25)=8/25.

Both endpoint fibers are therefore excluded. On the middle triangle
the cut is y>=h, so

    mu(S intersect H_A)=c(1-h)^2.                       (7)

For H_B, the inequality on K_- is x+y<=k-2<0, so that fiber is excluded.
On K_+ it is x+y<=k+2, which includes the whole triangle: its maximum
x+y is (4/5)s<1/50. On T the cap x+y<=k is a similar triangle.
Consequently

    mu(S intersect H_B)=c k^2+b=c(k^2+e).               (8)

These two fixed halfspaces cover every point of (4). If y>=h, the
point lies in H_A. If y<=h, equation (5) gives x+y<=k, so it lies in
H_B. Their boundary intersection meets the candidate segment, and
closedness covers the equality case as well.

It remains to check that both masses are strictly below the OC target.
Expansion gives

    (1-h)^2=4/9+(17/39)e+(289/2704)e^2,
    k^2+e=4/9+(17/39)e+(121/676)e^2.

The second expression is larger. Its exact gap below (3) is

    tau-(k^2+e)
      =e/117-(256/1125)eta-(121/676)e^2.                (9)

This is strictly positive. A certificate needing no decimal arithmetic
follows from (2):

    e/117 >= 9/(64000*117) > 1/1000000,
    (256/1125)eta < 1/4000000,
    (121/676)e^2 < (1/5)(1/6250)^2
                 =1/195312500 <1/100000000.

Thus (9) is greater than

    1/1000000-1/4000000-1/100000000
      =74/100000000>0.

Equations (7)-(9) prove that every point of the entire middle candidate
segment belongs to a closed halfspace of mass strictly less than (2/9)M.

## 4. The two endpoint centroid candidates are also bad

Use the closed halfspaces

    H_-={y-2(z+1)>=(2-s)(8/75)},
    H_+={y+2(z-1)>=s(8/75)}.                            (10)

The first contains (-1,g_-) on its boundary and excludes the other two
fibers, since their y coordinates are at most one and the integer tilt
subtracts at least two. It cuts K_- through its centroid parallel to
its horizontal edge, retaining exactly (4/9)a. Similarly H_+ isolates
K_+, contains (1,g_+) on its boundary, and retains exactly (4/9)b.

Because a<M/2 and b<M/2, both retained masses are strictly smaller
than (2/9)M. The containing-halfspace requirement holds exactly, with
no perturbation of the centroid.

## Conclusion and scope

Every point of G intersect (Z x R^2) has depth strictly below 2/9.
All fibers have positive area, all vertices and four bad halfspaces
are rational, the exact integer fibers have been checked, and the
whole continuum of middle candidates is covered by (6). Therefore
the convex hull of the actual fiber centroids can miss every OC point.

This is a counterexample only to that selector restriction. It says
nothing against existence of an OC point elsewhere in S.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_centroid_convex_hull_counterexample.py` independently
checks all triangle areas and centroids, all midpoint generators, all four
clipped cap areas, the exact segment equation, and every strict comparison
using rational arithmetic only. In actual area units it also checks
M/2-a=1/4096000. Dividing by c=area(T) doubles that gap.
